summary: Raising the payments-db statement timeout from 5s to 60s let a new reporting query hold connections until the pool was exhausted, taking checkout and orders down with it. Vigil classified it SEV1 on the shared-dependency rule and named the culprit commit within a minute.

timeline.event: Commit 40b61e74bd deployed: max_connections 40 to 180, statement_timeout 5s to 60s, plus an on-demand revenue rollup query.
ConnectionPoolExhausted alert fired for payments-db (0 idle connections for 4 minutes).
Vigil brief posted: SEV1 with blast radius checkout and orders, culprit 40b61e74bd at 0.84 confidence.
Incident marked resolved after the timeout change was rolled back and the running rollups were terminated.

root_cause: Commit 40b61e74bd disabled the effective ceiling on query duration by moving statement_timeout to 60s while adding a heavy orders-to-payments rollup that admins could trigger on demand. Concurrent rollups held connections for up to a minute each and starved every other client of the pool.
contributing_factors: max_connections was raised in the same change, masking the saturation until it was total.
The reporting query ran against the primary rather than a read replica.
impact: payments-db serves checkout, orders, and inventory; two user-facing services returned 5xx for the duration, against a 2,000 requests/minute database baseline.
resolution: Rolled back 40b61e74bd to restore the 5s statement timeout and terminated the in-flight rollup queries with pg_terminate_backend.
went_well: Severity came from the service catalog, so a non-user-facing database still paged as SEV1 with its two user-facing dependents named.
The connection-pool runbook section matched the failure exactly.
went_poorly: A timeout change and a new expensive query shipped in one commit, so neither could be rolled back alone.
Pool saturation had no warning-level alert before total exhaustion.

action_items.description: Move the revenue rollup to a read replica with a dedicated connection budget.
Add a warning alert at 80% payments-db pool utilisation.
Require timeout and pool-sizing changes to ship separately from query changes.
